title: QTR Sprint Canvas for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Diego Morales
description: Objective: Produce a compact, actionable quarterly sprint canvas that aligns Hosted API launch lanes with curated model-catalog commitments. This ticket scopes the planning work to create a prioritized delivery plan, risks & mitigations, canary windows, and OKR mappings for Q2. Scope includes: 1) defining 3 release lanes (Core Latency, Cost-Optimized, Safety-Checked models), 2) canary gating criteria and rollback triggers, 3) cross-team staffing and capacity hedges for Dedicated vs Hosted, 4) evaluation/quality signal sets and observability dashboards required for rollout decisions. Out of scope: model training, billing pricing changes, and on-prem packaging work. Success metrics: a) Sprint canvas approved by PM + Eng leadership by 2026-02-12; b) Runbook and canary checklist published; c) Acceptance test suite (eval prompts + perf baselines) integrated into CI; d) Identify capacity commit plan for Dedicated with required GPU-hours and cost delta estimates.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas includes prioritized features and mapping to OKRs with owners
Canary gating criteria documented with concrete signal thresholds (latency/quality/error-rate)
A minimal evaluation prompt set and baseline results stored in the eval harness (link provided)
Cross-team dependency table with committed dates and contingency lanes
Stakeholder sign-off from Console, Runtime, and Security teams

notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive canary thresholds reduce exposure but increase false-positive rollbacks; we chose conservative quality gates for Safety lane and relaxed latency gates for Cost lane to allow quantized variants. Staffing trade-off: Runtime needs a 0.4 FTE commitment for kernel tuning during canaries; Console needs a 0.25 FTE for dashboarding. Proposal: Timebox tuning to 3 sprints and re-evaluate in retro.
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize canvas and OKR mapping; publish canary gating signals. Week 2-3: Instrument eval harness and baseline runs; Runtime to finalize kernel selection table for prioritized models. Week 4: Dry-run canary with internal traffic and simulate Dedicated capacity shortage. Week 5-8: Staged canaries (Latency lane -> Cost lane -> Safety lane), capture metrics in Console dashboards. End of Quarter: Retro and decision: promote lanes to GA or schedule follow-ups for Q3.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Model-quality regressions after quantization. Mitigation: keep quality gate strict (BLEU/ROUGE proxies + human spot checks) and holdback a 5% traffic slice for comparison. Risk: Dedicated capacity procurement delay. Mitigation: predefine hosted fallback variants and communicate timing SLA to sales. Risk: Security dependencies for Private customers. Mitigation: defer Private Safety rollout to Q3 and provide transparent timeline.
